name: jasna
one_liner: A tool that automatically finds blurred or pixelated patches in a video and fills them back in with GPU-generated detail, leaving the rest of the footage untouched.
buyer: Hard to name a legitimate business buyer here: the real user base is individual hobbyists paying small one-off 'supporter' fees for better models, drawn largely from the community this tool is purpose-built to serve — removing mosaic censorship from adult video.
business_use_cases: An individual hobbyist pays 15 to 25 dollars for the supporter models to get sharper restoration on personal video files.

A restoration enthusiast experiments with it on old damaged or low-resolution archival footage, though the project's own training and audience are built around mosaic censorship specifically, not general archival repair.

Any commercial use beyond the creator's own one-off license sales is thin, since platforms and payment processors heavily restrict monetizing this category of content, leaving no defensible path to build a real business on top of it.

money_ideas.idea: The creator's own model: one-time supporter license fees for better restoration models, sold directly to individual users.

steal_this: Don't build a business on this one. It's a technically solid hobby project for a legally and ethically gray niche with real consent and platform-policy risk, not a foundation to start a company on.
